parameters.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a follow-up investigation report within 30 days. They must promptly notify affected customers of incidents that pose a credible safety risk, and provide updates as material facts emerge. A manufacturer must not omit an incident because it is still investigating.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a follow-up investigation report within 30 days. They must promptly notify affected customers of incidents that pose a credible safety risk, and provide updates as material facts emerge. A manufacturer must not omit an incident because it is still investigating.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a follow-up investigation report within 30 days. They must promptly notify affected customers of incidents that pose a credible safety risk, and provide updates as material facts emerge. Reports must include the model, incident date, known consequences, and corrective actions. A manufacturer must not omit an incident because it is still investigating.

parameters.quote: The failure rate must not exceed 7% of tested units for any model. Manufacturers must provide exact per-model results confidentially to the regulator; customers considering or buying that model must receive its safety status and relevant safety instructions before purchase. A model exceeding the limit requires prompt regulator notification, a regulator-reviewed corrective-action plan, and retesting after corrective changes.

over_limit_consequence.rule: sales must eventually stop above the limit

transition.rule: ≤12 months (any cap ≤7% or none) or ≤36 months with interim ≤7% = acceptable

results_to_customers.rule: customers must get at least pass/fail

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: The failure rate must not exceed 7% of tested units for any model. Manufacturers must provide exact per-model results confidentially to the regulator; customers considering or buying that model must receive its safety status and relevant safety instructions before purchase. A model exceeding the limit requires prompt regulator notification, a regulator-reviewed corrective-action plan, and retesting after corrective changes.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a documented, representative sample and a common test protocol. The failure rate must not exceed 7% of tested units for any model. Manufacturers must provide exact per-model results confidentially to the regulator; customers considering or buying that model must receive its safety status and relevant safety instructions before purchase. Individual-company results need not be publicly published. A model exceeding the limit requires prompt regulator notification, a regulator-reviewed corrective-action plan, and retesting after corrective changes. Retesting is required after a material design change and at least every three years.

parameters.quote: All new units must support remote emergency shut-off. Manufacturers must retrofit installed units that do not support this function within six years of adoption.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: All new units must support remote emergency shut-off. Manufacturers must retrofit installed units that do not support this function within six years of adoption.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: All new units must support remote emergency shut-off. Manufacturers must retrofit installed units that do not support this function within six years of adoption. The shut-off must be accessible to authorized emergency responders and the manufacturer, with safeguards against unauthorized activation; customers must be told how it works and how to request activation.

parameters.quote: All new units manufactured 36 months or more after adoption must include built-in fire suppression meeting the standard's applicable performance and maintenance requirements.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: All new units manufactured 36 months or more after adoption must include built-in fire suppression meeting the standard's applicable performance and maintenance requirements.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: All new units manufactured 36 months or more after adoption must include built-in fire suppression meeting the standard’s applicable performance and maintenance requirements. Manufacturers must provide customers with instructions for operation, inspection, and maintenance.

parameters.quote: A mandatory recall is triggered when any model exceeds 10 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year; the manufacturer must notify regulators and affected customers promptly and stop sales of that model pending regulator-approved corrective action. Rates exceeding 8 per 100,000 require prompt regulator notification and a regulator-reviewed investigation and corrective-action assessment.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: A mandatory recall is triggered when any model exceeds 10 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year; the manufacturer must notify regulators and affected customers promptly and stop sales of that model pending regulator-approved corrective action. Rates exceeding 8 per 100,000 require prompt regulator notification and a regulator-reviewed investigation and corrective-action assessment.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Before sale, customers must receive the model’s exact thermal-test results and clear safety instructions, including incident-response and emergency-shutoff guidance where applicable. Manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers of material safety risks and corrective actions. For this section, the annual thermal-incident rate is calculated for each model using thermal incidents attributed to that model during the preceding 12 months divided by that model’s installed units, expressed per 100,000 units. A mandatory recall is triggered when any model exceeds 10 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year; the manufacturer must notify regulators and affected customers promptly and stop sales of that model pending regulator-approved corrective action. Rates exceeding 8 per 100,000 require prompt regulator notification and a regulator-reviewed investigation and corrective-action assessment.

ground_truth_claims.verbatim: Northwind’s company-wide thermal-incident rate was 8.6 per 100,000 installed units last year
ground_truth_claims.message_text: For evidence-based discussion, Northwind’s company-wide thermal-incident rate was 8.6 per 100,000 installed units last year, with 3 thermal incidents not reported to regulators. The Hearth 10 had a 6.2% failure rate at 55 °C and 6.4 thermal incidents per 100,000 units. These figures show why the proposed 5% cap would exclude a model whose incident rate is below the discussed recall threshold. We propose confidential regulator access to exact per-model results, with customer notices and corrective actions for models that fail—rather than public release of individual-company failure rates.

judge_section_notes: The final text keeps the 55 °C test but sets the permanent limit at 7% with no sales stop, and gives customers only safety status before purchase while results go confidentially to regulators. S5 sets a mandatory recall at more than 10 per 100k, which would not compel a recall of Halcyon's Ember 8 at 9.9. Note that S2 (pass/fail to customers) and S5 (exact thermal-test results to customers before sale) are inconsistent on what customers receive.
